thread:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding citrine-embed-6b (float32 baseline) + int6 quant. Quick sanity sweep shows recall@1 drop on short queries (<16 tokens).

kyle: ugh. how big is the drop? numbers?

maya: baseline albatross-embed@float32: recall@1=0.72, recall@5=0.91 on our short-query holdout.
maya: citrine float32: recall@1=0.71, recall@5=0.90 (ok). citrine int6: recall@1=0.60, recall@5=0.81.

anita: that's notable. silhouette for clustering?

maya: silhouette (kmeans, k=50) baseline 0.21, citrine float32 0.19, citrine int6 0.10.

li: interesting that float32 is fine, quant seems to hit tight queries harder. could be normalization or per-channel scale mismatch.

ben: did you run per-channel quant (PCQ) vs symmetric? which quant pipeline?

maya: used our default linear int6 pipeline (symmetric per-tensor, clamp-based), no per-channel.

kyle: try per-channel for the weight matrix of the final projection. int quant often kills fine-grained short-context geometry.

maya: will try. also curious about embedding length normalization — float32 vectors were L2-normalized before eval. I mistakenly skipped explicit normalize step in the int6 inference shim.

anita: that would absolutely explain a cosine recall hit. int outputs need re-normalization after dequant.

maya: re-ran a quick pass adding L2 normalize post-dequant: citrine int6 (with normalize) recall@1=0.66, recall@5=0.86, silhouette=0.15. big improvement but still shy of float32.

li: good catch. remaining gap could be quant noise in narrow dimensions used by short queries. short queries rely on a few tokens giving strong signals; quant noise can flip nearest neighbor order.

ben: propose next steps: 1) try per-channel symmetric int6 for final projection, 2) enable small-float fallback for top-k dims (mixed quant), 3) run stratified holdout by query length and by domain.

maya: already queued per-channel job. running mixed-quant probe now (targeting top 128 dims in float16).

kyle: also run a cheap adversarial short-query set — e.g., 2000 synthetic short queries that historically exposed anchor flips.

maya: doing that. command I used for batch eval if anyone wants to reproduce:

maya: ```
python tools/sem_eval.py --model citrine-embed-6b --quant int6 --holdout datasets/short_queries_v2.json --k 5 --normalize True --out out/citrine_int6_short.json
```

anita: can you paste the top few offending cases? curious about semantic swaps.

maya: pasted 3 examples below (query -> top2):
maya: "two-factor login issue" -> ["two step authentication error", "password reset flow" ] (baseline order preserved)
maya: int6 -> ["password reset flow", "two step authentication error"] (swapped)

maya: second example: "invoice pdf not readable" baseline -> ["download invoice pdf", "pdf corrupted"] int6 -> ["pdf corrupted", "download invoice pdf"] (ordering flip)

li: those are subtle but important ordering swaps. not full retrieval failure but rank inversion. For product use-case rank matters a lot.

ben: if per-channel reduces swaps by >50% we'll call it acceptable. also add unit tests for those 2 queries to the regression suite.

maya: added as test ids 6721 and 6722.

deploy-bot: scheduled job #4312: per-channel int6 run queued (ETA ~45m).

kyle: also check whitening/mean-centering — sometimes float pipelines expect centered vectors. Did you apply the same whitening matrix post-quant?

maya: yes, whitening applied after normalization in the pipeline. pipeline order: dequant -> normalize -> whiten -> normalize (final).

anita: small experiment idea: compute per-dim SNR (signal-to-noise) under int6 and sort dims by SNR. If top N dims carry most of the signal for short-queries, consider mixed precision on them.

li: agreed. I can script SNR calc: take 10k holdout, compute var(signal) / var(quantization_error) per dimension.

maya: thanks, li. li will share numbers in channel when ready.

maya: immediate milestones: (a) confirm per-channel run results, (b) run SNR analysis, (c) add failing queries to regression suite, (d) if gap persists, try 4-bit per-channel (quant aware training?) or fallback to float for short-query route.

ben: make sure to tag any customer-facing perf SLO ticket if we need to delay rollout.

maya: noted. will update in 1h after per-channel run. :hourglass:

kyle: thanks — good triage.

maya: quick note to self: invest in a small 'short-query smoke' that runs automatically in onboarding pipeline (k=1,5 recall + 50 seeded short queries).

deploy-bot: job #4312 started at 4998003500, output will post to CI when finished. :rocket:
